title: 1990 AHSME Problem 14
statement: An acute isosceles triangle, \(ABC,\) is inscribed in a circle. Through \(B\) and \(C,\) tangents to the circle are drawn, meeting at point \(D.\) If \(\angle ABC=\angle ACB=2\angle D\) and \(x\) is the radian measure of \(\angle A,\) then \(x=\)

solutions.text:
The two base angles are each \(\frac{\pi-x}{2}.\) The minor arc \(BC\) has central angle \(2x,\) so the angle between the tangents is \(\pi-2x.\) The given relation yields \[ \frac{\pi-x}{2}=2(\pi-2x). \] Therefore \(7x=3\pi,\) or \(x=\frac{3\pi}{7}.\)

Thus the correct answer is A.
